newsitem.title: USA: U.S. panel may advise splitting immigration service.
newsitem.headline: U.S. panel may advise splitting immigration service.

text.p: A U.S. advisory panel may recommend next month splitting the Immigration and Naturalisation Service into three separate parts, a congressional source said Tuesday.

Outlines of the proposal were reported in Tuesday's New York Times but U.S. officials noted that it was still a draft, and the recommendations from the U.S. Commission on Immigration Reform could change before the final report is issued Sept. 30.
The draft report calls for splitting the INS into three parts. The Justice Department would maintain control of U.S. borders and stemming illegal immigration.
The State Department would handle immigration services, including citizenship requests. And the Labour Department would address rules about foreign workers.
The Justice Department has opposed splitting the INS, one of its agencies.

"We think juggling the boxes is not the answer. The task is to identify the problems and improve INS performance as we have been working to do that for several years," said Justice spokesman Bert Brandenburg. He said the department has not seen the commission's draft report.

Allen Kay, a spokesman for Representative Lamar Smith, a Texas Republican who heads the House Immigration Subcommittee, said Smith has been briefed on the proposals to date but has "not taken a position" on the idea of splitting the agency. He said Smith wants to complete a thorough review of the INS.
